name: How Walkable Does This Sidewalk Look? 360° sidewalk-view walkability rating
description:
Faithful replication with the paper's own stimuli: 100 of the 974 sidewalk-view 360° panoramas (footpath.ai) that the authors released on Hugging Face (mdamandeh/user-conditioned-walkability-assessment), drawn at random and resized to 1920×960. Based on Damandeh & Saberi, "Walkable to Whom? Capturing Subjective Variability in Walkability Perception Using Multimodal Deep Learning" (arXiv:2608.06934). Participants first report age, gender, current place of residence, childhood residential environment, walking frequency, country of upbringing and any disability affecting walking. They then rate a block of 25 interactive 360° panoramas (drag to look around) on the paper's prompt, "On a scale of 1 (poor walkability) to 5 (excellent walkability), how walkable does this environment appear to you?", with the paper's walkability definition behind an information icon. The original survey collected 29,870 ratings from 1,196 Australian respondents (Pureprofile panel, about 10 minutes) across urban, suburban and regional sidewalks. If the image provider or authors object to this use, the template will be taken down.

Differences from the original study: (1) 100 images instead of the 974-image pool, and each participant's 25 images are drawn at random rather than by round-robin blocks balanced across urban, suburban and regional settings; (2) the two repeated consistency-check images are not included; (3) answer options for the background questions are our own wording, since the paper lists the questions but not their categories.
author: Damandeh & Saberi
